# Installed native diagnostic

The dedicated `codex/installed-native-qualification-20261003` push route uses a standard windows-2022 runner, its existing VS 2022/v143 x64 environment, and exact product source f92d28016fc74e5076591173b4ac5518415fed2f. Orchestration is checked out separately at the workflow SHA. This is a Windows Server diagnostic, not Windows 11 certification, MSI qualification or publication. Root schedules it only after the current Primary Release capture job terminates.

No dependency installer, cache service, MSI transaction or signing command is included. Missing preinstalled prerequisites fail. The Shipping preset remains authoritative; only BUILD_TESTS is enabled to expose two benign incompatible-module fixture targets. Explicit product targets include SparkWorker and preserve the complete installer component inventory. Build project parallelism is one; the installed SDK consumer retains its existing parallelism two.

Steps run sequentially and stop at the first failed qualification. Existing overall bound: 240 minutes; build step 185, SDK 30, ABI 5, closure 15 minutes, with the overall cap authoritative. No cold-run completion or RAM estimate is claimed. The ABI step adds samples and redist to the SDK test's component prefix; it never installs an MSI. The positive SDK test precedes those additions. Host image equality before/after component staging binds both runs to the same binary; closure's independently staged graphs must contain that same host hash. Build host, reference DLL/sidecar and two fixture DLL/sidecar hashes are checked before and after later phases. The ABI driver additionally checks its own input mutation and native rejection contracts.

Identity records distinguish source SHA/tree/submodules from workflow SHA/helper digest. Host records include OS/image, tool paths/file versions/hashes, SDK/toolset and available memory. Version logs supplement tool file metadata. Each passing phase writes its own binding record; their absence or any failure record prevents claiming complete qualification. There is no final release readiness promotion.

The always-run collector allowlists only top-level identity/binding/failure files and phase logs, SDK runtime logs, ABI reports/case logs and closure graphs/logs. It excludes all installed files, user data and build products. JSON proof is retained in full or collection fails; log tails are limited to 16 KiB with original size/hash recorded. Total text must fit 900000 bytes and a local preview ZIP must fit 1000000 bytes, leaving headroom under a 1 MiB artifact archive limit. Upload uses only the frozen diagnostics-text directory, never a nested ZIP. Retention is one day. Full build logs remain ephemeral on the runner; tails are deliberately diagnostic, not a full build transcript. Cancellation at the overall timeout may prevent artifact collection; never infer success from missing evidence. The helper requires a short ASCII evidence child of RUNNER_TEMP disjoint from source and never recursively deletes directories; the existing SDK runner receives only that run's fresh sdk child.

Source-only tests: `python -B Tests/Tools/test_installed_native_runner.py`. All subprocesses used by orchestration tests are mocked; synthetic files are not native module qualification. Tests cover SDK command/cwd/timeout, initial and installed host mismatch, failure propagation, samples/redist/ABI sequencing and report binding, closure graph multiplicity/hash, archive exclusion/tails and oversized proof rejection.

Process lifetime is owned through the exact product source `tools/docs_contract.py` kill-on-close Windows job adapter. A Python wrapper waits on stdin; commands start only after successful job assignment and a GO handshake. Assignment failure releases no command. Success, failure and timeout all close the owned job, then allow at most ten seconds to reap the wrapper. No process-group fallback permits unowned compilation. Every phase shares a monotonic deadline thirty seconds below its unchanged workflow step ceiling; later commands receive only the remaining budget. Git identity reads are also bounded and contained. Mock contracts cover assignment-before-release, fail-closed assignment, normal/failure/timeout job closure, wrapper handshake and deadline exhaustion. These are source checks, not validation of hosted nested-job availability.
